title: Corner Brook Home Rebates 2026: Older Homes, Oil to Heat Pump, Insulation
desc: Corner Brook home rebates for 2026: up to $22,000 to switch from oil to a heat pump, takeCHARGE insulation and air sealing for older homes, and no-cost upgrades for lower incomes.
lead: Corner Brook has some of the oldest housing of any city in the province. Older homes lose more heat, so they get the most from insulation, air sealing and getting off oil. Here is what is open on October 16, 2026 for Corner Brook homeowners.
cards_heading: What is open in Corner Brook in 2026
cards_intro: We read the takeCHARGE and Government of Newfoundland and Labrador pages on October 16, 2026. Each card links to its source.

cards.title: Heat pump (switching from oil)
cards.note: Oil or propane homes switching to a central heat pump, income-qualified. Up to $9,000 for others. Paid to your installer.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: 75% of the cost for attic and basement, plus labour. Electric heat, home built before 2014.

cards.title: Air sealing
cards.note: Based on blower door results. Electric heat and an HRV or air exchanger needed.

cards.title: HRV
cards.note: Eligible model, HRAI certified installer, any heat source.

cards.title: No-cost upgrades
cards.note: TakeCharge Greener Homes Program for income-qualified homeowners.

cards.title: Oil heating supplement
cards.note: Bought 250 litres of oil in 2026, family income $150,000 or less. Apply by January 15, 2027.

sections: What Corner Brook homes look like

The 2021 Census counted 8,870 households in Corner Brook. About 65% of homes were built before 1981, compared with about 50% across the province, and about 30% were built before 1961. About 3,420 households, roughly 39%, own a detached house built before 1981. About 62% of households own their home and 38% rent.

Source: Statistics Canada, 2021 Census, table 98-10-0233-01.

Newfoundland Power is the main electricity distributor on the island and has an area office in Corner Brook. All the takeCHARGE programs here are for Newfoundland Power and NL Hydro customers, so either utility works. Check the name on your bill when you apply.
Older house, electric heat: seal and insulate first

A house built before 1961 often has little attic insulation and leaky basement walls. takeCHARGE pays 75% of the insulation cost, up to $1,000 for the attic and $1,000 for the basement, plus up to $500 each for labour by a participating installer. If the old attic insulation has to come out, the rebate counts it as R-20 to start, and your installer can add air sealing at $0.50 a square foot up to $750. Your main heat must be electric.

Oil furnaces are common in older homes. Oil to Electric pays up to $22,000 for a central heat pump if your household is income-qualified (for example $73,600 or less for two people), or up to $9,000 if not, and pays to remove the oil tank. In an old house, ask your installer about the backup heat the program requires and about your panel: the program also covers a panel upgrade where needed. Apply for the Home Heating Supplement ($200 to $500) this winter too.

With 38% of households renting, landlords matter here. Landlords can switch up to two rental homes through Oil to Electric, and the TakeCharge Greener Homes Program lets landlords apply for up to two homes if the tenants are income-qualified. Income-qualified homeowners can get upgrades at no cost through the same program. It is separate from the old federal Canada Greener Homes Grant, which has ended.
claim_steps: Check what heats your home and whether your income is under the line.
Lower income: apply to TakeCharge Greener Homes first.
Electric heat: book insulation and air sealing with a participating installer.
Oil heat: apply for the Home Heating Supplement, then get Oil to Electric quotes.
faq: Can I get a heat pump rebate in Corner Brook?
Yes, if you heat with oil or propane: up to $22,000 for a central heat pump when your income qualifies, or up to $9,000 if not, through Oil to Electric.
My house is from the 1950s. What should I do first?
If it has electric heat, insulation and air sealing usually come first: takeCHARGE pays up to $3,000 for insulation and up to $750 for air sealing. If it has oil heat, look at Oil to Electric.
Does the City of Corner Brook have its own rebate?
We found no City of Corner Brook home energy rebate.
Yes. Landlords can do up to two rental homes through Oil to Electric, and through Greener Homes if tenants are income-qualified.
